why: The copy's second sign of mḫe is a clear C (ḫ), not a 3; no divider is drawn before pisoẖte.
The copy shows a cross-shaped sign with a dot between b and r that the type does not have; kept as t?.
The copy leaves a clear gap after yi.
The copy has a fully hatched sign at (15) before p; the type counts none.
The copy has two strokes marked sic where the type has i.
No i after t in the copy; the names table also has none.

The copy draws a divider between the two words.
No sign between p and to in the copy; Griffith himself queries the o.
